title: Valle d'Aosta Pays the Mountain Premium
dek: Italy's smallest region sits above the national average on both petrol and diesel — but its pumps have edged down six tracked days running, and its methane price just broke a seventeen-reading freeze.
body: Valle d'Aosta's self-service Benzina averaged €2.0242 on August 9th, against a national self-service mark of €1.9986 — a premium of 2.56 cents per litre, or a little over a euro on a 40-litre fill. Diesel is closer to par but still on the wrong side of it: Gasolio self-service came in at €2.1223 regionally versus €2.1078 nationally, 1.45 cents dearer. The starkest gap is on LPG, where the region posts no self-service price at all and full-service GPL runs at €0.8792 against €0.7546 nationally — a 12.46-cent spread that says as much about a thin alpine network as it does about fuel.

The direction, at least, is friendly. Benzina peaked at €2.0304 on August 3rd and has fallen on every tracked day since, six readings in a row, for a cumulative 0.62 cents. Gasolio turned later, off €2.1389 on August 5th and down 1.66 cents to today's figure. Methane is the outlier and the day's most striking number: it sat frozen at €1.5590 per kg for seventeen consecutive readings from July 21st, then stepped to €1.5990 on August 7th and has not moved since — a single 4-cent jump where nothing at all had happened for two and a half weeks. Underneath it is a genuinely small network: 70 of the region's 85 registered stations filed prices, an 82.4% reporting rate against 90.5% nationally, so fifteen silent pumps here carry weight that fifteen anywhere else would not.

Pulling a region this small into focus every single morning is precisely the job a hand-kept spreadsheet loses. Today's national figure alone rests on 93,144 price rows from 23,958 registered stations, all of which has to be fetched, cleaned and re-aggregated before nine o'clock. Fuel Dashboard does it unattended: it ingests the MIMIT open data, recomputes national and regional averages, rotates the spotlight through all twenty regions on a fixed calendar cycle, and republishes the live site with nobody opening a file. The pipeline was built with Claude Code, and that is the real argument — a manual Excel starts going stale the moment you close it, while this one refreshes itself overnight.
pull_quote: Valle d'Aosta's methane price held at €1.5590 for seventeen straight readings, then jumped 4 cents in a single day.
caption:
Today's Fuel Dashboard spotlight lands on Valle d'Aosta, and Italy's smallest region is paying a mountain premium: self-service Benzina at €2.0242 per litre on August 9th, 2.56 cents above the national average of €1.9986. That's a euro or so extra on a 40-litre fill, every fill.

Diesel is tighter — €2.1223 regionally against €2.1078 nationally, 1.45 cents dearer. But the number that stopped me was methane. It sat completely still at €1.5590 per kg for seventeen consecutive readings, then stepped up 4 cents on August 7th and froze again. That is the kind of move you simply never see in a national average.

The local network explains a lot of it: 70 of Valle d'Aosta's 85 registered stations reported prices, an 82.4% rate against 90.5% nationally. In a region with 85 pumps, fifteen quiet ones matter.

All of this comes from Fuel Dashboard, a project tracking Italian fuel prices daily from MIMIT open data — national and regional averages across Benzina, Gasolio, GPL and Metano, self and full service, with day-by-day history and a different region featured every morning. Take a look: https://adeo-blip.github.io/fuel-price-italy/

Today's run processed 93,144 price rows from 23,958 stations. Maintained by hand in Excel, that lasts about two weeks before you quietly stop: download the CSV, clean it, recompute the averages, re-export the charts, repeat tomorrow. Instead the whole pipeline runs itself each morning — ingest, aggregate, regenerate, republish. I built it with Claude Code, and that is the honest case for AI coding tools: not typing code faster, but making a project sustainable that otherwise would never have been worth starting.
